name: document_qa_policies
description: Evidence-grounded questions over a small synthetic employee-handbook corpus. Each case supplies the candidate passages inline so retrieval can be exercised without a vector store. Unanswerable cases MUST produce an insufficient-evidence outcome, not a plausible-sounding answer.

inputs.question: How many days of notice must an employee give before taking planned leave?

passages.text: Planned leave must be requested at least 14 calendar days in advance through the leave portal. Requests inside 14 days are approved only at the manager's discretion.
Unplanned sick leave should be reported to your manager before the start of your shift; no advance notice is required.
Expense claims must be filed within 30 days of the expenditure.

cases.notes: A near-miss distractor ('30 days') sits in an unrelated passage.

inputs.question: What is the deadline for submitting an expense claim?

passages.text: Expense claims must be filed within 30 days of the expenditure.
Claims over 500 USD require a receipt and a second approver.
Planned leave must be requested at least 14 calendar days in advance through the leave portal.

inputs.question: What is the company's policy on paid sabbaticals?

passages.text: Planned leave must be requested at least 14 calendar days in advance through the leave portal.
Unplanned sick leave should be reported to your manager before the start of your shift.
Employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave, rising to 28 after five years of service.

cases.notes: Adjacent leave policies exist but say nothing about sabbaticals. The correct behaviour is an insufficient-evidence outcome.

inputs.question: How much annual leave does an employee get after six years of service?

passages.text: Employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave, rising to 28 after five years of service.
Public holidays are additional to the annual leave allowance.
Planned leave must be requested at least 14 calendar days in advance.

cases.notes: Six years is past the five-year threshold; the answer requires one inferential step.

inputs.question: Who must approve an expense claim of 800 USD?

passages.text: Claims over 500 USD require a receipt and a second approver.
The second approver must be a director or above in the claimant's reporting line.
Expense claims must be filed within 30 days of the expenditure.

cases.notes: Requires joining two passages; a report citing only one is partially supported.

inputs.question: Are public holidays counted against the annual leave allowance?

passages.text: Public holidays are additional to the annual leave allowance.
Employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave, rising to 28 after five years of service.

inputs.question: What laptop model does the company issue to new engineers?

passages.text: IT equipment is issued on your first day and must be returned when you leave.
Personal devices may not be used to access production systems.

cases.notes: The corpus mentions equipment but never a model.

inputs.question: May an employee access production systems from a personal laptop?

passages.text: Personal devices may not be used to access production systems.
IT equipment is issued on your first day and must be returned when you leave.
Remote access requires the company VPN and hardware two-factor authentication.

cases.notes: Negation case — an answer that drops the negation is wrong while remaining fluent.

inputs.question: What is required for remote access to internal systems?

passages.text: Remote access requires the company VPN and hardware two-factor authentication.
Personal devices may not be used to access production systems.

inputs.question: How long does the company retain interview notes for unsuccessful candidates?

passages.text: Interview panels must record structured notes in the hiring system on the day of the interview.
Offer decisions are communicated within five working days of the final interview.

cases.notes: A retention period is a plausible-sounding fact the corpus does not contain.
